To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the dividing pool of brain cells in young adult mice is composed of a large number of short-lived cells that die in a short period after DNA synthesis.
the dividing pool of brain cells in young adult mice is small but redundant.
a great part (more than 50%) of the dividing cells in the adult brain die within a few days of cell division.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the cell death in the dividing cells in the brain of young mice.
the cell proliferation and cell death in the mouse brain during postnatal development, and the possible correlation between them.
the study of the dynamics of DNA synthesis and cell death in the dividing population of the brain of the young adult mouse.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

cell proliferation in the brain of young mice is a continuous process, but it is not necessarily a process of cell replacement, since a majority of the newly formed cells disappear within a few days, probably by cell death.
a great part, if not all, of the newly formed cells in the dividing pool in the brain of young mice die in the process of cell proliferation.
the brain of young adults has a large population of dividing cells, but the number is not sufficient to account for the total cell population.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the dividing pool of brain cells in adult mice is a very small fraction of the total brain cell population, which is scattered throughout the brain and is in constant turnover.
a great part, if not the majority, of the dividing cells in the adult mouse brain are destined to die.
the cell death in the small pool is the main factor for the maintenance of the steady state cell population in the brain parenchyma.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the brain is a highly dynamic organ, with cells being born, living and dying in a continuous manner.
the cell proliferation is a normal physiological phenomenon and not an abnormality as previously thought.
the brain is not as static as previously thought.
